note: Only shared advertised-claim acceptance scenarios belong here. The same inputs and assertions run independently against upstream Python and .NET Linux/macOS/Windows. Multi-node scenarios keep upstream RNS as the fixed peer and replace only the candidate node; upstream-to-upstream is the baseline. Unimplemented scenarios remain visible, never inferred from integration tests.

contracts.title: Cryptographic addressing: derive the same destination from an imported identity and application name
contracts.source: README.md:38-39 (Notable Features: coordination-less globally unique addressing and identification)
contracts.acceptance: Persist the exact fixed 64-byte identity, and derive the independent fixture's rns.id destination hash.
contracts.boundary: One deterministic identity/name fixture; not a statistical uniqueness proof.

contracts.title: Cryptographic communication: produce Ed25519 signatures and decrypt authenticated identity ciphertext
contracts.source: README.md:46-53 (Notable Features: X25519, Ed25519 and encrypted tokens)
contracts.acceptance: Match independent fixture signature bytes and decrypted plaintext using identical keys and input files.
contracts.boundary: Fixture-level functionality, not a cryptographic audit or complete forward-secrecy acceptance.

contracts.title: Delivery confirmations: accept a proof and time out when the upstream destination supplies no proof
contracts.source: README.md:54 (Notable Features: unforgeable packet delivery confirmations)
contracts.acceptance: Fixed upstream RNS peer receives 16-byte probes at both destinations; candidate reports valid reply/0% loss with exit 0, and timeout/100% loss with exit 2 without a proof.
contracts.boundary: Direct loopback TCP; not a forged-proof, multi-hop or impaired-link acceptance test.

contracts.title: Authentication and virtual network segmentation on supported interfaces
contracts.boundary: Existing .NET-only IFAC/failure-isolation checks remain integration evidence.

contracts.title: Reliable bulk transfer with automatic sequencing, compression and checksumming
contracts.boundary: Existing native and mixed-peer resource flows remain integration evidence; not multi-gigabyte acceptance.

contracts.title: Self-configuring multi-hop transport over heterogeneous carriers
contracts.boundary: Existing mixed-mesh checks do not automatically pass this row.

contracts.title: Lightweight, flexible application request/response exchanges
